title: Focus returns to the opener and moves on when a focused card leaves
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept") has four Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17701) and {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17702) led by {Technician-A}, {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17703) led by {Technician-B}, and {Work-order-4} (for example S10043-17704) with no lead technician.
  • Tech View and Board View offer the Technician filter after Assigned to me.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Click once in the Search box, then put the mouse aside: from here on use only the keyboard, except where a step says to click.
  5. Press Tab until the first card in {Technician-A}'s column has focus, and write down which work order it is.
  6. Press Tab until that card's More actions (…) button has focus, and press Enter.
  7. Press Escape and look at what has focus.
  8. Press Enter, move to Reassign lead technician with the arrow keys or Tab, and press Enter.
  9. Press Escape and look at what has focus.
  10. Click the Technician filter, tick {Technician-A} and press Escape.
  11. Click once in the Search box, then press Tab until the first card in {Technician-A}'s column has focus.
  12. Press Tab until its More actions (…) button has focus, press Enter, move to Reassign lead technician and press Enter.
  13. Type the first letters of {Technician-B}'s first name, move to {Technician-B}'s row with the arrow keys or Tab and press Enter.
  14. Look at what has focus.
  15. Do steps 12 and 13 again for the card that now has focus, picking {Technician-B} again.
  16. Look at what has focus.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 7: the menu closes and focus is back on the card's More actions (…) button, the control that opened it.
  • Step 9: the dialog closes without changing anything, and focus is back on the card's More actions (…) button, the control from which the menu and the dialog were opened.
  • Step 14: the reassigned work order leaves the board, because {Technician-B} is not chosen in the Technician filter, and focus moves to the other card in {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Step 16: with no card left in {Technician-A}'s column, focus moves to {Technician-A}'s column header.
  • Steps 7 to 16: focus is always visible and you can carry on with the keyboard alone.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 54 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S11-R5, S11-R6, S11-E1, S11-E2 and S1-R15, read 15 Oct 2026. The QA lead's decision of 12 Oct 2026 (focus at the top of the page after a page refresh is accepted while the focus design is pending) no longer applies, because the focus rules are now written. Focus after a technician becomes inactive while you work (S11-E2) cannot be set up by hand: the board shows that change only after a page reload, which starts focus at the top of the page, so it is not checked in this case. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 28, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 15 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/12/2026, before the expected results changed on 15 Oct 2026; the changed results have not yet been checked against a build.

Until 15 Oct 2026 Story 11 only listed keyboard behaviour the design still had to define, so this case asked the tester to try keys and write down what each did. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. PRD version 54 rewrites Story 11 into these requirements, and this case now checks them.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R5: “Escape closes an open menu, dialog or tooltip without changing anything.”
  • S11-R6: “When a menu or dialog closes, focus returns to the control that opened it.”
  • S11-E1: “When the focused work order leaves the result (for example after a filter change or a reassignment), focus moves to the next row or card in the same group or column, or to that group or column header when none is left.”
  • S11-E2: “When a technician becomes inactive and their group or column is no longer shown, focus moves to the next group or column header.”
  • S1-R15: “In Tech View and Board View the filter bar also offers a Technician filter, after Assigned to me. It is a multi-select listing Unassigned first, then the location’s technicians (the same people who get a group or column, S9-R4), by first name then last name. Choosing one or more shows only those technicians’ groups or columns; every other group or column, pinned ones included, is hidden. It filters by lead technician only.”
  • Story 11 user story: “As a keyboard user, I want to navigate work orders and their actions so that these controls are usable without a mouse.”
